summary: The 49ers traded a 2024 third-round pick to the Commanders for pass rusher Chase Young before the 2023 deadline, and the article argues he may not be a pure rental. Although San Francisco projects to have little 2024 cap space, it can create room by releasing Randy Gregory and restructuring contracts. Young's market value is projected near Rashan Gary's deal, and the team has few key free agents, so his arrival looks more like an audition.
one_line: Despite thin projected 2024 cap space, the 49ers have ways to create room, making Chase Young's trade more of an audition than a rental.
key_facts: The 49ers traded a 2024 third-round pick to the Commanders for Chase Young ahead of the 2023 trade deadline.
Young was the No. 2 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft and had five sacks and 18 pressures in eight games in 2023.
Washington traded both top defensive ends, Young and Montez Sweat; Young reunites with college teammate and fellow No. 2 pick Nick Bosa.
The 49ers defense ranked 22nd in sacks per game at 2.3.
OverTheCap lists the 49ers with just $1,479,772 in 2024 cap space, seventh-least in the NFL.
Releasing Randy Gregory would open $14 million in cap space with no dead-cap hit, since he has no guaranteed money left.
Ten other active players have 2024 cap hits of at least $14.1 million and could restructure or extend; Trent Williams has the highest at $31.7 million.
Spotrac projects Young at about $17.8 million annually on a four-year deal, which the article considers light.
Rashan Gary's Packers extension is four years, $96 million, $24 million AAV, with $34.6 million guaranteed; Young could hypothetically top $100 million on the open market.
The franchise tag was worth just under $20 million last season, but one-year deals are harder to fit into limited cap space.
Only 15 other 49ers are set to be free agents in 2024, and just Tashaun Gipson and Clelin Ferrell are full-time starters.
The article concludes Young's acquisition is more of an audition to remain with the 49ers than a pure rental.
